chunks: And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali who said: I asked Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both,
about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who give what they give while their hearts are filled with fear' (23:60),
He said: Out of their compassion and hope — they fear that their deeds may be rejected if they disobey, and at the same time they hope that their deeds might be accepted from them.

key_terms.رجاء: Raja' — hope, expectation of good; the counterpart to fear in the balanced spiritual life of a believer
key_terms.شفقة: Shafaqa — compassion, tender fear; a gentle anxiety born of love and concern rather than terror
key_terms.وجلة: Wajila — trembling with awe, fearful; describes the inner state of sincere believers who perform good deeds yet remain anxious about their acceptance

ai.seo_question: What does Quran 23:60 mean about hearts filled with fear according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) interprets Quran 23:60, explaining that the 'fear' (wajal) in the hearts of the believers described in this verse stems from a dual spiritual state: they fear that their deeds may be rejected due to disobedience, while simultaneously hoping for divine acceptance. This teaching was given to a student named Ali who asked the Imam directly about the meaning of this Quranic verse.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 28. And with the first chain of narration, from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘Ali who said: I asked Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him
about the verse from the Qur’an: ’And those who strive with righteous deeds to the greatest extent and their hearts are filled with fear....’ (al-Mu’minoon. 23:60).
He said: "That is their fear and hope. They fear that their acts may be rejected because of their sins, and at the same time, hope that they might be accepted from them."
